title: Review of c07's ringswim at 256^2 (SIMD): replicates on fresh seed 12 (117 persistent splits, generation 19, 96 segments >= 3 BL, no band); mu=0 at the same size divides but never swims
summary: Ran world.py (256^2) on seed 12 with labkit (T=20000) and the author's celltrack.py, and celltrack with mu=0 at the same size and seed. World: from noise, a bounded population of 25-76 walled cells (occupancy 0.20 at the end) swims as crescents and divides to t=20000 with no domain-wrapping band (sheet); celltrack 117 persistent splits, max generation 19, 331 splits vs 229 merges, 96 segments >= 3 BL and 19 >= 5 BL. mu=0: 110 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges, 0 segments >= 3 BL. labkit's L link rim/core 1.49 (140/209 membrane-like), just below the aggregate gate, as the claim says.

observations.S: rerun/seed12/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole 256^2 domain
observations.I: rerun/seed12/sheet.png: discrete walled cells and crescents t=800-20000, no band
observations.M: celltrack_summary.txt: 96 segments >= 3 BL, 19 >= 5 BL; mu=0 at matched size and seed: 0

verdicts.limitation: Genealogy remains reticulate (229 merges per 331 splits; labkit's coarse tracker finds 0 persistent splits), and the motile arm's high generation count partly reflects fusion-fission cycles; the mu=0 twin divides cleanly (0 merges) but only to generation 4 because cells there are static and stop growing. I did not check the named track 604 or make a strip.
